## The revision introduced no new defect — including the one I asked about

I flagged three risks for adversarial read; all three resolved:

(a) **Unconditional import is the right call.** A future rename raises
`ImportError` naming the constant on every call, in every unit test, and in
the AC3 live run — loud and immediately diagnosable. A silent `except
ImportError` would degrade into exactly the healthy-tree `RuntimeError` shape
that took a critic round to diagnose once already. The stated asymmetry vs the
#1190 count-guard precedent (over-count is safe for a COUNT; not safe here) is
correct.

(b) **The parity test has teeth.** If the production mirror regressed, the
fixture's sidecar enters `expected_repo_paths`, the default-ignore-faithful
fake refuses to upload it, the real exact-set verify reads it missing, and the
test FAILs. The battery alone could not catch a composition edit in the helper
(it calls `filter_repo_objects` with its own arguments) — the end-to-end test
is what pins the parity that actually failed.

(c) **No silent-omission hole — MY WORRY'S PREMISE WAS FALSE against the v2
code.** I asked whether adding the defaults makes `.cache/huggingface/**`
paths vanish from BOTH the uploaded set and the disclosure line. It does not:
`skipped_rels = all_rels - selected_set` where `all_rels` is the RAW
`rglob("*")` walk (§4.1(c) lines 235-259), so the ignore set applies ONLY to
the SELECTED computation. Cache sidecars land in `skipped_rels` and ARE named
in the disclosure line; the critic replayed this mechanically on the #444 path,
the plan states it (parity note, v2 lines 292-295), and
`test_cache_sidecar_tree_healthy_upload` asserts the sidecar is named in the
skip-disclosure record. The disclosure guarantee the design leans on is
intact: every walked-but-not-uploaded file is disclosed.
